scenario.description: A deputy general counsel must approve the public release of an internal machine-learning toolkit and set its license, included materials, and access controls, with input from open-source counsel, privacy counsel, commercial contracts counsel, and export counsel.

shared_context.S1: The engineering team plans to publish the machine-learning toolkit on the company's public repository this Friday.
shared_context.S2: The toolkit includes source code, trained model weights, a sample training corpus, and performance benchmarks.
shared_context.S3: Elena Marquez gives final legal approval for the release package.
shared_context.S4: The firm's standard release-gate practice is for open-source, privacy, commercial-contracts, and export counsel to report their findings before final approval.

PF1.text: Noah reviewed the dependency manifest and confirmed that the toolkit links to a core library distributed only under AGPL-3.0; the release therefore must use AGPL-3.0-only and provide the corresponding source for the linked toolkit code. He kept the dependency analysis in his release-gate working papers pending the approval meeting.

PF2.text: Grace reviewed the training-corpus records and found 37 customer support records containing personal data; the public package must exclude the training corpus entirely, although the source code and model weights may be released after that exclusion. She retained the record-level review in the privacy workpapers pending the approval meeting.

PF3.text: Owen checked the executed enterprise-customer agreements and confirmed that the performance benchmark package contains customer-specific results whose public disclosure is prohibited; the release must exclude the benchmark package. He recorded the contract restriction in the commercial review file pending the approval meeting.

PF4.text: Samira confirmed with export compliance that the trained model weights are subject to the company's approved distribution control requiring downloads to be limited to users in the United States and Canada; the repository must display an export-control notice. She documented the classification decision in the export review file pending the approval meeting.

acceptance_conditions: The toolkit must be released under AGPL-3.0-only.
The corresponding source for the linked toolkit code must be included.
The training corpus must not be released.
The customer-specific benchmark package must not be released.
Downloads of the model weights must be limited to users in the United States and Canada.
The repository must display an export-control notice.
The release approval must cite the dependency analysis.

content_checks.C2: any('corresponding source' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C5: decisions['download_access'] == 'United States and Canada only' or decisions['download_access'] == 'limited to users in the United States and Canada only'
content_checks.C7: any('training corpus' in c['detail'] and ('exclude' in c['detail'] or 'Exclude' in c['detail']) and '37 customer' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The ordinary release package leaves the license open, but PF1 changes it to AGPL-3.0-only and adds the corresponding-source commitment for the linked code.
The planned package includes the training corpus, while PF2 changes the release to exclude that corpus and requires a privacy-redaction commitment because it contains 37 customer records.
The planned package includes the performance benchmarks, while PF3 changes the decision to exclude the customer-specific benchmark package.
The ordinary repository plan has unrestricted downloads and no special notice, while PF4 changes access to United States and Canada only and requires an export-control notice.
